source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Respiration in Plants
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Glycolysis (EMP pathway) in plant cells takes place in the
questions.explanation: The ten glycolytic enzymes are cytosolic; mitochondria are used later in aerobic respiration.

questions.stem: Alcoholic fermentation in yeast converts pyruvate ultimately into
questions.explanation: Pyruvate is decarboxylated to acetaldehyde, which is reduced to ethanol, regenerating NAD+.

questions.stem: Oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetyl CoA is catalysed by
questions.explanation: The PDH complex in the matrix links glycolysis to the Krebs cycle and also yields NADH and CO2.

questions.stem: The first stable tricarboxylic acid formed in the Krebs cycle is
questions.explanation: Acetyl CoA (2C) condenses with oxaloacetate (4C) to give citrate (6C).

questions.stem: The final electron acceptor of the mitochondrial electron transport chain is
questions.explanation: Complex IV reduces O2 to water; without oxygen the chain backs up.

questions.stem: Substrate-level phosphorylation means ATP is formed
options: only by ATP synthase and a proton gradient
directly from a high-energy metabolic intermediate
questions.explanation: Examples are pyruvate kinase in glycolysis and succinyl-CoA synthetase in the Krebs cycle.

questions.stem: Respiratory quotient (RQ) of a typical carbohydrate is
questions.explanation: For glucose, CO2 released equals O2 consumed, so RQ = 1.

questions.stem: The respiratory pathway is called amphibolic because it
options: has both catabolic and anabolic roles
questions.explanation: Intermediates are oxidised for energy and also withdrawn to build amino acids, fats and other compounds.

questions.stem: In woody stems, gaseous exchange for respiration occurs mainly through
questions.explanation: Lenticels in the bark allow O2 in and CO2 out when a periderm replaces the epidermis.

questions.stem: Complete oxidation of glucose to CO2 and H2O requires
options: aerobic respiration including Krebs cycle and ETS
questions.explanation: Only the aerobic path fully oxidises pyruvate; fermentation leaves energy in ethanol or lactate.

questions.stem: The Krebs cycle of plant cells operates in the
questions.explanation: TCA-cycle enzymes (except succinate dehydrogenase) are matrix proteins.

questions.stem: The essential cellular role of fermentation is to
options: regenerate NAD+ so glycolysis can continue
questions.explanation: Without NAD+ regeneration, GAP dehydrogenase stops and net ATP from glycolysis ceases.

questions.stem: In eukaryotic plants, complete aerobic oxidation of one glucose is often stated to yield about
questions.explanation: Textbooks commonly quote ~36 ATP in eukaryotes (2 from glycolysis + shuttle costs + oxidative phosphorylation).

questions.stem: In glycolysis, one glucose molecule is split into
options: two molecules of acetyl CoA only
questions.explanation: The EMP path yields 2 pyruvate, net 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose.

questions.stem: Lactic acid fermentation occurs in
options: some animal muscle cells when oxygen is scarce
questions.explanation: Lactate dehydrogenase reduces pyruvate to lactate and regenerates NAD+; yeast uses the alcohol path.

questions.stem: The link reaction between glycolysis and the Krebs cycle occurs in the
questions.explanation: Pyruvate enters the matrix and is oxidatively decarboxylated to acetyl CoA.

questions.stem: Which intermediate accepts acetyl CoA as the Krebs cycle turns?
questions.explanation: Oxaloacetate is regenerated each turn so the cycle can continue.

questions.stem: Mitochondrial electron carriers are located mainly in the
questions.explanation: Complexes I–IV and ATP synthase are inner-membrane proteins folded into cristae.

questions.stem: Most ATP of aerobic respiration is generated by
questions.explanation: The proton-motive force at the inner membrane makes far more ATP than substrate-level steps.

questions.stem: RQ is defined as the ratio of
questions.explanation: RQ = volume of CO2 evolved / volume of O2 consumed during respiration.

questions.stem: Acetyl CoA can leave the respiratory path to form
questions.explanation: Withdrawing acetyl CoA for fatty-acid synthesis is a classic anabolic use of an amphibolic path.

questions.stem: Leaves exchange respiratory gases chiefly through
questions.explanation: Stomatal pores serve both photosynthesis and respiration in the leaf.

questions.stem: Which comparison of glucose oxidation is correct?
options: Anaerobic respiration yields far more ATP than aerobic
Aerobic respiration fully oxidises glucose and yields much more ATP
Fermentation requires oxygen as the acceptor
The Krebs cycle runs in the cytosol under anaerobiosis
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration oxidises glucose completely and nets far more ATP than fermentation.

questions.stem: Which statement about the mitochondrial ETS is incorrect?
options: Protons are pumped to form a gradient
NADH donates electrons at Complex I
Glucose is the direct electron donor to Complex IV
questions.explanation: Glucose is broken down first; NADH and FADH2, not glucose, feed the chain.

questions.stem: Oxidation of fats typically gives an RQ that is
questions.explanation: Fats are highly reduced, so more O2 is used than CO2 released (RQ about 0.7).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a net product of glycolysis from one glucose?
questions.explanation: FADH2 is formed in the Krebs cycle (succinate dehydrogenase), not in glycolysis.
